overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 7
overview.text: Students wrote and solved algebraic expressions and equations based on verbal statements for linear and exponential equations in Modules 1 and 3. In this lesson, students apply the same ideas to solving quadratic equations by writing expressions to represent side lengths and solving equations when given the area of a rectangle or other polygons(A-SSE.B.3a). A-CED.A.1 is central to the concepts of this lesson, as students create equations from a context and solve using the techniques they have developed in the early lessons of this module.
outcomes: Students interpret word problems to create equations in one variable and solve them (i.e., determine the solution set) using factoring and the zero product property.

MP.2MP.2Throughout this lesson, students are presented with a verbal description where a relationship can be modeled algebraically. Students must make sense of the quantities presented and decontextualize the verbal description to solve the basic one-variable quadratic equations. Then, they contextualize their solutions to interpret results and answer the questions posed by the examples.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 7 Exit Ticket: Creating and Solving Quadratic Equations in One Variable
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

The perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. If the length is 2 cm more than a number, and the width is 5 cm less than twice the same number, what is the number?

A plot of land for sale has a width of x ft. and a length that is 8 ft. less than its width. A farmer will only purchase the land if it measures 240 ft^{2}. What value for x causes the farmer to purchase the land?
exitTicket.solution:
The perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. If the length is 2 cm more than a number, and the width is 5 cm less than twice the same number, what is the number?

2l+2w=P2(n+2)+2(2n-5)=546n-6=54n=10

A plot of land for sale has a width of x ft. and a length that is 8 ft. less than its width. A farmer will only purchase the land if it measures 240 ft^{2}. What value for x causes the farmer to purchase the land?

(x)(x-8)=240x^{2}-8x-240=0(x-20)(x+12)=0x=20 or x=-12

Since the answer cannot be negative, the answer is x=20. The farmer will purchase the land if the width is 20 ft.

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Creating and Solving Quadratic Equations in One Variable through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt:
Solve the following problems.

The length of a rectangle is 2 cm less than its width. If the area of the rectangle is 35 cm^{2}, find the width.
problems.solution:
(w-2)(w)=35w^{2}-2w-35=0(w+5)(w-7)=0w=7 or-5

However, since the measurement can only be positive, the width is 7 cm.

problems.prompt: The ratio of length to width (measured in inches) in a rectangle is 4∶7. Find the length of the rectangle if the area is known to be 700 in^{2}.
problems.solution:
(4x)(7x)=70028x^{2}-700=028(x^{2}-25)=028(x+5)(x-5)=0x=5 or-5

However, the measure can only be positive, which means x=5, and the length is 20 inches.

problems.prompt: One base of a trapezoid is three times the length of the second base. The height of the trapezoid is 2 in. smaller than the second base. If the area of the trapezoid is 30 in^{2}, find the lengths of the bases and the height of the trapezoid.
problems.solution:
A=\frac{1}{2}(b_{1}+b_{2})h30=\frac{1}{2}(3b_{2}+b_{2})(b_{2}-2)30=(2b_{2})(b_{2}-2)2b_{2}^{2}-4b_{2}-30=02(b_{2}-5)(b_{2}+3)=0b_{2}=5 or-3

However, only the positive value makes sense. The first base is 15 in.; the second base is 5 in.; and the height is 3 in.

problems.prompt: A student is painting an accent wall in his room where the length of the wall is 3 ft. more than its width. The wall has an area of 130 ft^{2}. What are the length and the width, in feet?
problems.solution:
(w+3)(w)=130w^{2}+3w-130=0(w+13)(w-10)=0w=10 or-13

However, since the measure must be positive, the width is 10 ft., and the length is 13 ft.

problems.prompt: Find two consecutive even integers whose product is 80. (There are two pairs, and only an algebraic solution will be accepted.)
problems.solution:
(w)(w+2)=80w^{2}+2w-80=0(w+10)(w-8)=0w=8 or-10

So, the consecutive even integers are 8 and 10 or -10 and -8.
